en.title: Bérénice Bejo Stars as Cinema's Forgotten Pioneer in New HBO Max Series
en.summary: Oscar-nominee Bérénice Bejo is set to embody Alice Guy-Blaché, the groundbreaking first female fiction filmmaker, in a sweeping new HBO Max and France Télévisions drama. The six-part series promises to unearth the incredible, long-overlooked story of a true cinematic visionary.
en.body:
Few figures in cinema history have been as profoundly overlooked as **Alice Guy-Blaché**. Now, thanks to an ambitious new HBO Max and France Télévisions co-production, her extraordinary life and groundbreaking work are finally set to receive the spotlight they deserve. Starring Oscar-nominee **Bérénice Bejo** (known for her captivating performance in **The Artist**), the six-part series, simply titled **Alice**, will chronicle the journey of the world's very first female fiction filmmaker.

Born in France, Guy-Blaché began her career in the late 1890s, working for Léon Gaumont. She quickly proved her mettle, not only directing films but also experimenting with sound and color technologies that were revolutionary for the era. Despite founding her own studio in the United States and producing hundreds of films, her legacy was largely overshadowed by her male contemporaries and eventually erased from historical accounts. This series, created by **Tim Loane** and **Claire Lemaréchal**, and co-directed by **Virginie Verrier** and **Guillaume Lonergan**, aims to rectify that historical injustice, tracing her path from Paris to New York and early Hollywood.

## A Visionary Rediscovered

The production is already underway, with filming taking place across France, Belgium, and Canada through December. The choice of **Bérénice Bejo** to portray Guy-Blaché feels particularly fitting. Bejo possesses a rare ability to convey both vulnerability and steely determination, qualities essential for bringing a pioneering woman who navigated the male-dominated world of early filmmaking and entrepreneurship to life. The series promises to explore the immense obstacles Guy-Blaché faced, not just as a filmmaker but as a woman striving for recognition and artistic control in a rapidly evolving industry. Her story is one of defiance, innovation, and an unyielding passion for the nascent art form of cinema.

## Why This Matters to Cinephiles

For passionate film fans, the **Alice** series represents more than just a historical drama; it's a chance to reclaim a vital piece of cinematic heritage. For too long, the narrative of early cinema has been told almost exclusively through the lens of men. **Alice Guy-Blaché** was not just *a* filmmaker; she was *the* filmmaker who arguably set the template for narrative cinema. Her innovations in storytelling, special effects, and even the very concept of a film studio were foundational. The fact that her contributions were marginalized and forgotten is a stark reminder of how easily history can be rewritten by those in power. This series offers a powerful corrective, celebrating a true visionary whose influence, though often uncredited, is deeply embedded in the DNA of filmmaking today.

## What's Next

With filming currently in progress, the **Alice** series is slated for release in 2026 on HBO Max and France Télévisions. Details regarding the specific premiere date and further casting announcements are expected to be revealed as production continues. Fans eager to learn more about the life and work of this forgotten pioneer will want to keep a close watch on official updates.
